decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:20938-P010-A20938-P005-L20938-P006-H20938-P007-H20938-P003-E20938-P009-1stProposed CGIsSustainable Drainage Strategy Dated May 2025Biodiversity Net Gain/loss Assessment Dated July 2025Construction Management Plan Dated 7 May 2025Bat Emergency Survey Dated May 2025Preliminary Bat Roost Assessment Dated April 2025Energy and Sustainability Statement Dated 05/05/2025Transport statement dated April 2025Tree Survey & Constraints Plan Dated 10/06/2025Post Construction Swept Path Analysis Swept Path Analysis - 7.5 BOX VANSwept Path Analysis - AXLE TIPPERSwept Path Analysis - CONCRETE TRUCKReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to the commencement of above-ground works of the development hereby permitted, full details of the external materials and finishes shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details. The submitted details shall include the following:o	External materials specification and samples, including manufacturer details, for all facing materials;o	Brickwork, including bond, joint, mortar and detailing such as soldier courses, lintels, curves, and the construction of a 1m × 1m bespoke sample panel on site for officer inspection;o	Roof materials and detailing, including tiles, parapets, edges, ridges, eaves, and all roof junctions;o	Windows and doors, including frames, operable function, window bars, and minimum reveal depth of 1 brick (215mm);o	Balustrades, refuse store, and rainwater goods;o	Soft and hard landscaping, including access paths and boundary treatments;o	Green roof, solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, and air source heat pump (ASHP) enclosures;o	External lighting;o	Detailed drawings at 1:20 and 1:5 scale to illustrate all of the above where appropriate.Reason: To ensure the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and that it protects thecharacter and appearance of the surrounding area.

No development including site preparation works, demolition or construction work shall commence until a Demolition and Construction Management Plan has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.       The Plan shall include the following: i.	details of the routing of construction vehicles to the site, hours of access, access and egress arrangements within the site, onsite car parking arrangements and security procedures; ii.	site preparation and construction stages of the development; iii.	details of provisions for recycling of materials, the provision on site of a storage/delivery area for all plant, site huts, site facilities and materials; iv.	wheel washing facilities; measures to control the emission of dust, noise and vibration arising from demolition and construction works; v.	noise mitigation measures for all plant and processors; vi.	details of a community liaison contact for the duration of all works associated with the development. The approved Demolition and Construction Management Plan shall be adhered to throughout the demolition and construction period for the development.Reason: Development must not commence before this condition is discharged to avoid hazard and obstruction being caused to users of the public highway to safeguard residential amenity from the start of the construction process.

Prior to the commencement of any works, a Dust Management Plan (DMP), based on an Air Quality and Dust Risk Assessment (AQDRA), shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the local planning authority. The DMP shall be in accordance with The Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG 2014. The DMP will need to detail the measures to reduce the impacts during the construction phase. The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan.During each four construction sub-phases of the proposed development (demolition, earthworks, construction, and trackout), PM10 continuous monitoring shall be carried out on site. Parameters to be monitored, duration, locations and monitoring techniques must be approved in writing by the London Borough of Enfield prior to commencement of monitoring. Reason: To protect the local amenity from demolition/construction dust.

Prior to the commencement of the development, evidence of site registration at http://nrmm.london/ to allow continuing details of Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) and plant of net power between 37kW and 560 kW to be uploaded during the construction phase of the development shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. Evidence that all plant and machinery to be used during the demolition and construction phases of the development shall meets Stage IV of EU Directive 97/68/ EC for both NOx and PM emissions shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. During the course of the demolitions, site preparation and construction phases, an inventory and emissions records for all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) shall be kept on site. The inventory shall demonstrate that all NRMM is regularly serviced and detail proof of emission limits for all equipment. All documentation shall be made available for inspection by Local Authority officers at all times until the completion of the development. Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and protecting public health

Prior to the occupation of the development the following documents, as necessary, must be submitted in writing and approved by the Local Planning Authority: A)	A Desk Study including a preliminary risk assessment which identifies: All previous uses; Potential contaminants associated with those uses; A conceptual site model indicating sources, pathways and receptors; and Potentially unacceptable risks arising from contamination at the site. B)	Should the desk study identify the need, a Site Investigation scheme to provide information for a detailed assessment of the risk to all receptors that may be affected, including those off site. The results of the site investigation to be summarised via a generic or detailed quantitative risk assessment with conclusions and recommendations for clear actions, where required. Reason: To ensure that contaminated land is properly treated and made safe safeguard the health and safety of the future occupants in accordance with policy 2.1.8 of the London Plan (2016) and CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

If required, a Remedial Options Appraisal and/or Remediation Strategy giving full details of the remediation and mitigation measures required and how they are to be undertaken. Where remediation is required, i) a Verification Plan setting out the details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy are complete to a satisfactory standard; and ii) A Monitoring and Maintenance Plan, setting out provisions for long-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action. iii) the development in the relevant Phase shall not be occupied until a post completion remediation Verification Report for that Phase, including results of sampling and monitoring carried out, has first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the site remediation criteria have been met. Reason: To ensure that contaminated land is properly treated and made safe safeguard the health and safety of the future occupants in accordance with policy 2.1.8 of the London Plan (2016) and CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with Section 5 (Recommendations) of the Preliminary Bat Roost Assessment, Report No. ASW/API/008/29/2025, April 2025. The approved measures shall be fully implemented prior to occupation of the development and thereafter retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To protect and enhance biodiversity in accordance with national and local planning policy.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the measures set out in Section 5 (Recommendations) of the Bat Emergence Survey, Report No. ASW/API/017/29/2025, May 2025. The approved measures shall be implemented in full and thereafter retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To protect bats and their habitats, in accordance with national and local planning policies relating to biodiversity and nature conservation.

Prior to the occupation of the development, a detailed Energy Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall demonstrate how the development incorporates measures to improve energy efficiency and reduce carbon dioxide (CO"²) emissions beyond the baseline requirements of Building Regulations Part L (2021) or any subsequent updates in force at the time of approval.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained and maintained as such thereafter.Reason:  In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that carbon emission reduction targets are met in accordance with the Local Development Plan, the London Plan (2021) and the NPPF (2024).

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate shall be submitted to an approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  Reason:  In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Core Strategy, relevant energy policies of the London Plan (2021) and the NPPF (2024).

Prior to first occupation of the development, details of the internal consumption of potable water shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Submitted details will demonstrate reduced water consumption through the use of water efficient fittings, appliances and recycling systems to show consumption equal to or less than 105 litres per person per day for the residential uses.  The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details so approved and maintained as such thereafter.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Policies CP21 of the Core Strategy (2010) and DMD 58 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Prior to first occupation of the development, details of all boundary treatments and means of enclosure shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The boundary treatment to the site frontage shall, where feasible, comprise soft evergreen hedging unless otherwise agreed in writing. Where a brick wall is proposed, the details shall demonstrate visual interest to break up the mass and add character, for example through patterning (such as herringbone detailing), variation in brick bond, texture, material, or colour treatment.The approved boundary treatments shall be installed prior to first occupation of the development and shall thereafter retained and maintained.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development and to safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition, site clearance and all preparatory work), an auditable schedule of arboricultural supervision and inspection of tree protection measures by a suitably qualified arboriculturist shall be provided. This will include, but not be limited to, supervision of all stages within the RPA of T004 horse chestnut and T013 plane.Upon the completion of each supervision visit, the findings and agreed actions / timescales arising from them shall be reported to the LPA by the arboriculturist by way of summary report supplemented with photographs where appropriate.The condition shall not be discharged until it has been demonstrated that compliance with the agreed AMS has been satisfactorily achieved.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and ensure compliance with the agreed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS), to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), ascheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved inwriting by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP) for each stage of the scheme. The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a. the preparation of the site access in the RPA of the retained horse chestnut tree T004 prior to any site deliveries, demolition or all other preparatory work. (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012).b. methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hardstanding and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c. the design and installation methodology of the proposed foundations for the construction which intrudes into theRPA of T004 horse chestnutd. location and installation of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retainedtrees and being compatible with the proposed planting;e. details of any construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;f. a full specification for the construction of all roads, paths, patios, parking areas and driveways (includingalterations to the existing layout of internal roads and hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base isspecified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical crosssection of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;g. detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-digsurfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated withprevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;h. a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;i. a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during bothdemolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of thefencing and extent of ground protection for each stage of the development;j. a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);k. details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment,materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;l. methods to improve the rooting environment for retained and proposed trees and landscaping.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of the hard and soft landscape treatment of all parts on the site not covered by buildings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The site shall be landscaped strictly in accordance with the approved details in the first planting season after completion or first occupation of the development, whichever is the sooner. Details shall include:1) a scaled plan showing all existing vegetation and landscape features to be retained including RPA and canopyspread of the trees) and trees and plants to be planted;2) location, type and materials to be used for hard landscaping including specifications, where applicable for:a. permeable pavingb. sustainable urban drainage integrationc. use within tree Root Protection Areas (RPAs);d. a schedule detailing sizes and numbers/densities of all proposed trees/plants;e. specifications for operations associated with plant establishment and maintenance that are compliant with bestpractice; and3) types, materials, design and dimensions of all boundary treatments including the boundary treatment to beintroduced between the pedestrian access and the disabled parking bays.There shall be no excavation or raising or lowering of levels within the prescribed root protection area of retained trees other than has already been agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Unless required by a separate landscape management condition, all soft landscaping shall have a written five-year maintenance programme following planting.Any new planting (other than trees) that is removed or becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced with new planting. Unless further specific permission has been given by the Local Planning Authority, replacement planting shall be in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with theBiodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and the Publication London Plan.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans, prior to completion or first occupation of the development hereby approved,whichever is the sooner; full details of all proposed tree planting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include:a. Planting, maintenance and aftercare specifications, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or otherprotective measures and confirmation of location;b. species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier and defect period. All tree planting shall be carried out inaccordance with those details and at those times;c. tree pit design (where appropriate) and;d. underground modular systems (where appropriate).All details shall refer to, and be in accordance with, the relevant British Standards for nursery stock, supply, planting and establishment.Any trees that are found to be dead, dying, severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced in the next planting season by specimens of similar size and species in the first suitable planting season.Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with theBiodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and the Publication London Plan.

The development shall not be occupied un the refuse and recycling facilities as shown on the approved plans have been provided. The facilities shall be maintained and retained thereafter.  Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets

The development shall not be occupied until the cycle parking facilities shown on the approved plans have been fully provided. The cycle parking shall be provided in accordance with the approved details, shall be secure, covered, and easily accessible at all times, and shall thereafter be retained for the sole use of cycle parking.Reason: To promote sustainable modes of transport and to ensure adequate cycle parking provision, in accordance with Policy T5 of the Development Plan.

Prior to the commencement of above-ground works, a detailed Sustainable Drainage (SuDS) scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall follow the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy and include:o	Source control measures for all hardstanding and roof runoff, including permeable paving (which shall not be lined), to manage water quantity and improve runoff quality;o	Storage and discharge controls designed to achieve greenfield runoff rates for 1 in 1-year and 1 in 100-year (plus climate change) events, including consideration of two-stage orifice controls or other appropriate measures;o	Extensive treatment measures for silt control and reduction of blockage risk across the site, aiming for as close to 100% of hardstanding runoff as possible to pass through source control;o	Details of implementation and maintenance, demonstrating how all SuDS features will be installed, retained, and maintained for the lifetime of the development.The approved SuDS measures shall be fully implemented prior to the first occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To reduce the risk of flooding on-site and elsewhere, and to ensure the provision of sustainable drainage

Prior to the commencement of above-ground works, a Fire Safety Strategy for the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall include details of means of escape, fire detection and alarm systems, access for fire appliances, and fire-fighting equipment. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved strategy and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the safety of future occupants and the building in accordance with Policy D12 of the London Plan 2021

All windows in the side elevations at first floor level and above of the development hereby permitted shall be fitted with obscured glazing and shall be non-opening below 1.7 metres from internal finished floor level. The obscured glazing and non-opening restriction shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the developmentReason: to safeguard residential amenity

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any subsequent re-enactment), no development falling within Classes A, B, C, or E of Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Order shall be carried out without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: to safeguard residential amenity

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015, or any amending Order, no external windows or doors other than those indicated on the approved drawings shall be installed in the development hereby approved without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining properties.
